newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 22.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading.

* Philippine stocks are likely to be weaker following the Dow's overnight drop as the gains on Wednesday were a short-lived reaction to the U.S. Federal Reserve keeping rates untouched, said Sun Hung Kai Securities Phils vice-president Raul Ruiz.
* But BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said that there may still be some spillover buying.
* Trading volume is still seen below two billion pesos.
* On Thursday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index rose 39.59 points to 2,538.97.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday dipped 12.77 points to 7,290.69. PLDT's ADR rose by $0 1/8 to $55.
* Philippine agricultural growth is expected to rise to 4.7 percent this year from last year's 3.9 percent due to prospects of better rice harvests, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said.
* The Bureau of Agricultural Statistics said that the agriculture sector grew 4.22 percent in the first three months, up from 2.49 percent in the year-earlier quarter.
* Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said that the Philippine economy was still on track but cautioned against falling into the traps that brought financial problems to Thailand.
* Pilipino Telephone Corp said it had signed a syndicated loan worth $90 million with a group of foreign financial institutions.
* Port operator Asian Terminals Inc said its net income for the first nine months of its fiscal year ended March 31 rose to 1.61 million pesos from 1.35 million the same period last year.
* Globe Telecom and Digital Telecommunications Philipines Inc (Digitel) said they have signed an interconnection agreement linking their telephone networks.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said it had allowed real estate firm Interport Resources Corp to offer a one-for-one rights issue.
* The SEC said it was stopping share traders and brokers from trading on their personal account following complaints by individual investors.
* The Philippine Daily Inquirer reported that President Ramos said first quarter agricultural growth pointed to a robust economic growth this year despite the current gloom in the stock market.

* BusinessWorld said that the House of Representatives ways and means committee is amenable to the Senate proposal to gradually reduce the corporate tax to 30 percent while slowly raising the levy on dividends. The House version of a comprehensive tax reform bill called for a 35 percent corporate tax.

* The Philippine Star quoting Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) may not approve the scheduled exit of the Philippines from IMF tutelage in June due to disagreements in Congress on provisions of a comprehensive tax reform bill concerning corporate and working spouses tax exemptions. (MANILA CHRONICLE/TIMES JOURNAL)
* The peso closed lower at 26.374 to the dollar vs 26.373
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 20.03125 percent.
